column3: Defines the best دين through submitting one's face to Allah, doing good, and Abraham's upright way.
The call from a near place does not clarify seeking another religion, acceptance, or loss.
Directly explains non-acceptance of spending through disbelief and unwilling practice.
Pairs the call to Islam with the injustice of inventing falsehood against Allah.
Immediate covenant context anchors the surrounding demand to affirm and aid the confirming messenger.
Its command to seek the last abode and avoid corruption provides a secondary contrast in the use of what is given.
Ends with rejected faith leading to ruined works and loss in the last life; its legal setting is distinct.
Nearby warning that disbelief leaves Allah independent of all worlds sharpens the consequence frame.
A prayer for acceptance supplies a distinct, personal use of the acceptance language.
Immediate context: no ransom from those who die in disbelief will be accepted.
Divine nearness does not add to the verse's religion, acceptance, or final-loss claim.
Seeking the face of the highest Lord gives a focused orientation parallel to submission, without naming religion.
Denial of Allah's signs is explicitly linked to becoming among the losers.
Immediate sequel characterizes turning away after the covenant as deviation.
Seeking another god after divine favor supplies a concrete contrary posture to exclusive submission.
Explicitly joins completed religion with Allah's approval of Islam as religion.
Its mention of the last life and nearness adds little to the religion-and-acceptance argument.
The seating image and remote channel resonance do not bear on the focus.
Preferring the present life, obstructing Allah's path, and seeking its crookedness frame a contrary course.
A prior people's denial is too general; the channel link is not topical support.
Giving oneself for Allah's approval suggests devoted orientation, but not the verse's exclusion or acceptance claim.
Becoming among the losers after wrongful killing provides a concrete loss outcome.
Immediate parallel: it asks about seeking another دين while all creation submits and returns to Allah.
Allah's acceptance of repentance distinguishes a restorative acceptance from the focus's refusal.
Profession by mouths without believing hearts offers a relevant contrast between claim and inward faith.
Giving what one loves concerns righteousness, not the specified alternative religion or acceptance.
Seeking beyond a stated boundary marks transgression, a useful formal parallel to seeking other than Islam.
Associating partners nullifies work and makes one among the losers, reinforcing the final consequence.
Entry in peace and eternity does not clarify the excluded alternative.
The request that a foundational act be accepted shows acceptance is sought rather than presumed.
No intercession or compensation will be accepted on the decisive day, framing acceptance beyond substitution.
Immediate confession of all revelation and submission gives the positive stance before the exclusion.
Spending is declared unacceptable whether willing or unwilling because of persistent deviation.
Allah's acceptance of repentance provides the clearest contrasting mode of accepted return.
A response to a call to faith and plea for a good end is adjacent in theme but indirect.
Spending solely for Allah's face gives an intention parallel, without defining religion or final acceptance.
A family covenant and judgment scene does not add to the focus.
Rain and harvest imagery, despite channel resonance, is not evidence for the focus claim.
Even total worldly ransom is not accepted from disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection.
No compensation or intercession is accepted on that day; it independently reinforces final non-acceptance.
Immediate continuation depicts disbelief after faith and clear testimony as outside divine guidance.
Acceptance of an offering is explicitly tied to God-consciousness, giving a condition absent from mere offering.
Recognition of error is joined to fear of being among the losers, a penitential counterpoint.
Calls recipients of the Book to believe in confirming revelation, extending the surrounding messenger-confirmation frame.
Seeking a judgment other than Allah's is a close structural contrary to seeking another religion.
States that the دين with Allah is Islam, the direct doctrinal counterpart to the focus.
Immediate consequence of the surrounding rejection: a comprehensive curse.
Seeking Allah's bounty within pilgrimage is a different, permitted sense of seeking.
Identifies the straight, upright religion with Abraham's way and dissociation from association.
Its fear and present-versus-last-life contrast does not resolve the focus's claim.
Seeking bounty across night and day is unrelated to choosing a religion.
Guidance and misguidance are relevant outcomes but this case supplies no religion or acceptance link.
Differing speech and the channel resonance do not add topical evidence.
Spending for Allah's approval supports sincere orientation only indirectly.
The guidance/misguidance contrast is broad and does not specify the alternative path.
Righteous believers entering the righteous gives no distinct aid beyond the final-life frame.
Seeking divine bounty at sea is a different use of seeking.
Denial of the last encounter appears, but the narrative detail is remote from the focus.
The punishment day is a generic consequence, without the focus's religious criterion.
Injustice and repentance in a dispute offer only a remote branch-based resonance.
Its prohibition of what is dedicated to other than Allah gives a bounded contrary to exclusive devotion.
Timely repentance is a secondary counterpart to the question of acceptance.
Those invoked besides Allah themselves seek nearness to their Lord, undermining their status as alternatives.
Obeying against divine proof is called loss, but the prophetic dispute is indirect.
The political submission of peace does not define the religious submission in the focus.
Non-acceptance of testimony shows acceptance can be withheld under a stated moral condition.
Seeking Allah's bounty through the sea is a distinct, nonreligious seeking.
The greeting scene and channel resonance do not clarify the focus.
A plea for just judgment and straight path is only a general orientation parallel.
The terse statement about being unaccountable does not add a clear link.
The ruined garden image does not address the focus.
Seeking Allah's bounty through winds and ships is a different use of seeking.
The salutation upon Abraham supplies only a distant Abrahamic association.
The destructive act in the narrative does not clarify the focus.
Like 70:31, seeking beyond the stated boundary is transgression; it is redundant but still parallel.
Turning away from Abraham's way is self-foolishness, while he is among the righteous in the last life.
The condemned conduct and narrative challenge lack a specific relation to the focus.
Acceptance of the best of deeds alongside overlooking evil distinguishes graded acceptance from blanket approval.
Calling on another god without proof is joined to reckoning and the failure of disbelievers.
Testing truthfulness and falsehood is too general despite the channel connection.
Seeking Allah's bounty and approval while supporting Allah and His messenger gives a positive pursuit pattern.
Pursuit of the present-world harvest is contrasted with having no share in the last life.
A marriage prohibition and its condemnation do not materially clarify the focus.
Seeking Allah's bounty through seafaring is another nonreligious instance of seeking.
Directly names the people of the last life as the losers, though without the stated reason.
The call at morning and channel resonance have no clear topical contribution.
Disagreement after knowledge through mutual aggression helps contextualize religious divergence, but indirectly.
Present blindness leading to worse blindness and greater deviation in the last life reinforces consequence, not criterion.
The mission to a criminal people gives no distinct connection.
Obstructing Allah's path, seeking its crookedness, and denying the last life closely maps the contrary posture.
Its balanced request for present and last-life good and protection from fire supports the final-life horizon.
The later remembrance formula does not clarify acceptance or alternative religion.
The artery image has no relevant semantic link.
Choosing prison over an illicit summons offers a remote contrast of resisting an alternative call.
Receiving the record in the left hand signals final failure but adds no criterion.
The dawn raid image has no relation to the focus.
Marital waiting rules and belief reference do not add to the focus.
Love of the immediate and neglect of a weighty day supplies a secondary contrary orientation.
Reverent fear and a returning heart suggest a positive disposition, without the religion or acceptance statement.
Household eating and greeting regulations do not add to the focus.
Directly joins submitting one's face to Allah with doing good and a secure final return.
Abraham and Ishmael ask to be made submitting to Allah, extending the Abrahamic basis of the focus.
Abraham's immediate response to the command to submit gives a foundational positive counterpart.
Abraham and Jacob charge their descendants not to die except as submitters.
The call away from Jewish or Christian identity toward Abraham's upright way directly frames a rival religious claim.
Confessing all revelations and ending with submission provides a close positive formulation.
The command to enter Islam wholly is a direct, though differently framed, call to Islam.
Apostasy from religion and the nullification of deeds supply a close contrary consequence.
The speaker and followers declare submission of the face to Allah; this is among the closest positive parallels.
The disciples' belief and request to be witnessed as submitters continue the same surah's submission theme.
The call to worship none but Allah and take no lords besides Him supplies an exclusive-devotion frame.
Abraham is explicitly neither Jewish nor Christian but upright and submitting.
Those nearest Abraham are his followers, this prophet, and believers, reinforcing the Abrahamic alignment.
Commands following Abraham's upright way, directly continuing the surah's religion argument.
The command not to die except as submitters gives the enduring endpoint of the positive posture.
Disbelief in Allah and His messengers, and separating among messengers, contrasts with the comprehensive faith of 3:84.
Names that selective disbelief as true disbelief and attaches punishment.
Belief in Allah and all messengers without distinction gives the positive counterpoint to selective rejection.
The shared revelation frame, distinct prescribed ways, and return to Allah refine how religion claims are situated.
Apostasy from religion and Allah bringing another devoted people provide a contrary and replacement frame.
Calling the Messiah divine is marked as disbelief and loss of paradise, a concrete contrary devotion.
Forbids excess in religion and following desires, a secondary warning against religious deviation.
Belief in Allah, the prophet, and what was sent down supplies a positive messenger-recognition parallel.
The disciples' belief and self-identification as submitters repeat the submission vocabulary.
The command to be first among submitters and not among associators gives a direct exclusive-devotion stance.
Rejects calling on what neither benefits nor harms after guidance, a close contrary to seeking an alternative.
Turning the face exclusively toward the Creator and rejecting association offers a related orientation image.
Commands setting the face rightly and calling on Allah with religion made sincere for Him.
Names the religion of truth in a legal-political context; relevant but not a direct gloss on 3:85.
Allah sends His messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over other religion.
Disbelief after Islam supplies a direct contrary transition within the same vocabulary.
Moses' community is commanded to rely on Allah if they are submitters.
Commands worship of Allah alone and being among the believers, a close exclusive-devotion frame.
Restricts judgment to Allah, commands worship of Him alone, and calls that the upright religion.
Joseph asks to die as a submitter and join the righteous, linking submission and final outcome.
Contrasts those rejoicing in revelation with factions denying part of it; the religious dispute is indirect.
The proclamation of one God and a warning for people of understanding support exclusive worship.
States that the religion is continually due to Allah and asks whether any other should be feared.
Commands following Abraham's upright way and denies his association.
Calls to the Lord's way with wisdom; relevant to the path alternative but not acceptance.
Commands worship of Allah alone and identifies it as a straight path.
The recurring prophetic message is that none is worthy of worship except Allah, so worship Him.
Affirms one God and commands submission to Him, with good news for the humble.
Each community has a rite; the prophet is told to call to his Lord rather than yield to dispute.
States that Allah named the community submitters before and in this revelation.
Declares the community one community and Allah its Lord, countering religious fragmentation.
Depicts people fragmenting their religion into factions, each rejoicing in its own portion.
The queen's final submission is explicitly with Solomon to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
Calls for common belief in the revealed God and ends with collective submission.
Commands setting the face toward the upright religion and identifies it with Allah's originating disposition.
Commands turning to Allah, fearing Him, prayer, and avoiding association.
Submitting one's face to Allah while doing good is called grasping the firmest handhold.
Commands worship of Allah while making religion sincere for Him.
Declares that pure religion belongs to Allah and rejects intermediaries claimed to bring nearness.
Commands sincere worship with religion made exclusively Allah's.
Reiterates worshipping Allah with religion made sincere for Him.
Those who avoid false objects of worship and turn to Allah receive good news.
Commands turning back and submitting to Allah before punishment arrives.
Commands calling on Allah with religion made sincere for Him despite the disbelievers.
Forbids worshipping others besides Allah and commands submission to the Lord of the worlds.
Proclaims one God and commands uprightness toward Him.
Unifies Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus under one ordained religion and forbids division within it.
Commands uprightness, faith in all revealed books, and justice among people amid religious dispute.
Commands worship of Allah and identifies this as a straight path.
Those who say Allah is our Lord and remain upright are freed from fear and grief.
Distinguishes outward submission from faith entering hearts, clarifying that labels alone are insufficient.
Allah sends His messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over all religion.
Commands worship of Allah with religion made sincere, uprightness, prayer, and almsgiving; calls this the upright religion.
